body:
Thank you for asking

**CA(6228; 3, 196, 12) and CA(6402; 3, 197, 12).** The method is the randomized post-optimization of Nayeri, Colbourn and Konjevod (2013), `postop-nck2013`, in our own implementation, with one added greedy step: a row with few uniquely covered tuples is removed when those tuples can be moved into free cells of other rows. No tabu search was used. The words "tabu repair" in the class column of my `records.csv` are wrong for these two rows, and I will fix them in the next version of the deposit. Also, the post-optimization started from the fused arrays: CA(6253; 3, 196, 13) → fused CA(6251; 3, 196, 12) → 6228, and CA(6422; 3, 197, 13) → fused CA(6420; 3, 197, 12) → 6403 → 6402. The CA(6229; 3, 196, 12) named in the text was a separate run that deleted 22 redundant rows.

Tabu repair (row deletion plus tabu search on single entries, Nurmela 2004, `tabu-n2004`) was used only for CA(812; 3, 11, 8) and for the strength-two blocks CA(246; 2, 18, 14) and CA(285; 2, 18, 16) inside CA(5568; 3, 19, 14) and CA(6376; 3, 19, 16).

**hyperoval-poly2.** The hyperoval part is classical: for even q it gives an OA(q^3; 3, q + 2, q), Bush (1952), `oa-bush1952`. The added column, a line-polychromatic colouring of AG(2, q), and the extra rows are my own construction. It has no published source yet. It is Theorem 7.2 of my preprint "Covering arrays from line-polychromatic colourings of affine planes", doi:10.5281/zenodo.23787051, which has not been peer reviewed. The closest earlier construction I know of is Theorem 3.2 of Colbourn, Kéri, Rivas Soriano and Schlage-Puchta (2010)

Thank you for the clear answer.

CA(6228; 3, 196, 12) and CA(6402; 3, 197, 12) now cite postop-nck2013 in builds_on. Their construction text now says the post-optimisation is that of Nayeri, Colbourn and Konjevod (2013) in your implementation, with the added greedy step, started from the fused CA(6251; 3, 196, 12) and CA(6420; 3, 197, 12), and with no tabu search.

The four hyperoval-poly2 rows, CA(812; 3, 11, 8), CA(5568; 3, 19, 14), CA(5879; 3, 19, 15) and CA(6376; 3, 19, 16), now cite Bush (1952) for the hyperoval part and your preprint (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23787051) for the added column and the extra rows, noted as not yet peer reviewed. CA(812; 3, 11, 8), CA(5568; 3, 19, 14) and CA(6376; 3, 19, 16) also cite Nurmela (2004) for the tabu repair, as do the strength-two rows CA(246; 2, 18, 14) and CA(285; 2, 18, 16). Every change is logged in table/CREDIT_CORRECTIONS.csv.

One more question. CA(350; 2, 20, 17) and the strength-two blocks inside CA(1848; 3, 13, 10), CA(3098; 3, 15, 12), CA(9476; 3, 21, 17) and CA(9884; 3, 21, 18) also say "row deletion + tabu repair (waveJ_free/wj_sa2.py)". Is that the same tabu repair of Nurmela (2004)? If so they will cite it too.

Your comment seems to end after Colbourn, Keri, Rivas Soriano and Schlage-Puchta (2010). If there was more, please add it.

-Christopher

Thank you, Christopher. I am sorry that my comment was cut off, and also for one mistake in it.

1. A correction for CA(6228; 3, 196, 12) and CA(6402; 3, 197, 12). I checked the run logs again. My comment got the starting arrays wrong, and the construction text you had before was right. The post-optimisation did not start from the fused arrays. The chains are:

CA(6253; 3, 196, 13) → fused CA(6251; 3, 196, 12) → 22 redundant rows deleted (greedy deletion of rows whose tuples are all covered by other rows, with an exhaustive check after each step) → CA(6229; 3, 196, 12) → post-optimisation → CA(6228; 3, 196, 12).
CA(6422; 3, 197, 13) → fused CA(6420; 3, 197, 12) → 16 redundant rows deleted → CA(6404; 3, 197, 12) → post-optimisation → CA(6403; 3, 197, 12) → CA(6402; 3, 197, 12).
The post-optimisation logs start from N = 6229 and N = 6404. So I was wrong to say that the post-optimisation started from the fused arrays and that CA(6229; 3, 196, 12) belonged to a separate run: CA(6229; 3, 196, 12) was the starting array. The rest of what I said still holds. The post-optimisation is that of Nayeri, Colbourn and Konjevod (2013) in my implementation, with the added greedy step, and no tabu search was used. So postop-nck2013 in builds_on is correct. Only the construction text needs the deletion step back, for example: "... giving CA(6251;3,196,12); then 22 redundant rows deleted, giving CA(6229;3,196,12); then randomized post-optimisation of Nayeri, Colbourn and Konjevod (2013) in Bai XunDi's implementation, with an added greedy step (...), starting from CA(6229;3,196,12); no tabu search". For CA(6402; 3, 197, 12) it is the same with 16 rows, starting from CA(6404; 3, 197, 12), through CA(6403; 3, 197, 12).

2. Yes, it is the same tabu repair. Despite its name, waveJ_free/wj_sa2.py does no simulated annealing. It is row deletion with Nurmela-style tabu repair, in my own implementation, and it is the same program that produced CA(246; 2, 18, 14) and CA(285; 2, 18, 16). It deletes the row with the fewest uniquely covered pairs. Then it repeatedly picks a random uncovered pair, and among the rows that would cover that pair after a change to one cell, it makes the non-tabu change that leaves the fewest pairs uncovered. A changed cell may not be changed again during the next 7 moves (tabu tenure 8). If every such move is tabu, it changes a random row so that it covers the pair. The logs show that every strength-two block you name came from this program:

CA(350; 2, 20, 17), from OA(19^2; 2, 20, 19) fused twice (357 rows); it is also the block inside CA(9476; 3, 21, 17);
CA(116; 2, 12, 10), from 119 rows, inside CA(1848; 3, 13, 10);
CA(165; 2, 14, 12), from 167 rows, inside CA(3098; 3, 15, 12);
CA(357; 2, 20, 18), from 359 rows, inside CA(9884; 3, 21, 18).
So all of these rows may cite Nurmela (2004). CA(116; 2, 12, 10) and CA(165; 2, 14, 12) only equal the table values and do not improve them. This also means that "only" in my comment was too narrow.

3. Two smaller points I found while checking.

CA(5879; 3, 19, 15): you were right not to cite Nurmela here. Its block is the CA(255; 2, 18, 15) from C. J. Colbourn's projection construction (x = 1), used without fusion or search (my tabu run to shorten it did not succeed), and N = 16^3 − 2(16 − 15) + (15 − 8)·255 = 5879. So this row should cite proj-c2008 and credit Colbourn for the ingredient, as CA(5568; 3, 19, 14) does. It may also cite fuse-ckrs2010, for the one fusion step on the old columns.
CA(812; 3, 11, 8): the tabu repair took CA(816; 3, 11, 8) down to 812, so tabu-n2004 is right. If you like, the construction text could say "then row deletion + tabu repair (Nurmela 2004, own implementation) starting from our CA(816; 3, 11, 8)". The strength-two copies CA(76; 2, 10, 8) inside CA(816; 3, 11, 8), and CA(286; 2, 18, 16), the start of CA(285; 2, 18, 16), came from my own simulated annealing, so there is no other method to cite there.
4. The missing end of my comment. The text was cut off when I pasted it. The full last paragraph was:

"The closest earlier construction I know of is Theorem 3.2 of Colbourn, Kéri, Rivas Soriano and Schlage-Puchta (2010). For these rows you may prefer to cite the preprint rather than the data deposit."

You have done that already. One note: I took the theorem number from the authors' preprint, so the numbering in Discrete Appl. Math. 158 (2010) may differ.

Bai XunDi

Thank you, Bai. That is very clear, and the run log details help a lot.

I have made these changes to the table, each with a line in table/CREDIT_CORRECTIONS.csv.

1. CA(6228;3,196,12) and CA(6402;3,197,12). The construction text has the deletion step back. It now goes from the fused CA(6251) through the deletion of 22 redundant rows to CA(6229), and the post-optimisation starts from CA(6229). The same for CA(6402) with 16 rows, starting from CA(6404) through CA(6403). postop-nck2013 stays.

2. CA(350;2,20,17), CA(1848;3,13,10), CA(3098;3,15,12), CA(9476;3,21,17) and CA(9884;3,21,18) now cite Nurmela (2004) for the tabu repair.

3. CA(5879;3,19,15) now cites Colbourn's projection construction and credits him for the CA(255;2,18,15) ingredient, the same way as CA(5568;3,19,14). It also cites the fusion step, and the construction text gives the count N = 16^3 - 2(16 - 15) + (15 - 8)*255.

4. CA(812;3,11,8) now says row deletion and tabu repair (Nurmela 2004, own implementation) from your CA(816;3,11,8).

Thanks also for the note on the theorem number. I will keep the preprint citation.

I think this covers everything here, so I will close the issue. Please reopen it if I missed something.

-Christopher
